questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly and gradually add front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana can affect you within minutes and last two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation to stay close together while keeping space between riders. Use single-file formation when turning, entering or leaving a highway, or going through curves.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure firmly and smoothly, increasing it step by step.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing offers all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and from bad weather. They do not cause discomfort.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injury and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Which factor does not affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also affect it.

questions.question: As weight moves to the front of your bike while braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Do nothing. The weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, the weight of your bike moves forward to the front tire. Gradually increase the front brake pressure as this happens.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn your handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press gently on the handgrip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip then the left.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time and brake harder.
Do both actions at the same time, focusing mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good traction to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. When it starts to rain, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. This keeps you away from the wet center. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space on both sides. This gives you the best chance to stay in control if a wind blast pushes you.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you far from car doors that might open, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Use the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not touch the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle sticks, try twisting it back and forth several times. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes on slippery surfaces. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make them return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Ride slower at night.
Honk the horn repeatedly.
Avoid riding at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower at night.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night to be safe. Also increase your following distance, use the headlights of cars ahead to help you see, use your high beam (unless near other vehicles), and be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be careful. Your tires use some of their grip to make the turn. Less grip is left for braking.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on the motorcycle they were riding.

questions.question: If the rear wheel locks while you are braking on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then reapply it quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely. Even with a locked rear wheel, you can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and traveling straight.
